papers.title: A type theory for invertibility in weak $\omega$-categories
papers.abstract: We present a conservative extension ICaTT of the dependent type theory Catt for weak $\omega$-categories with a type witnessing coinductive invertibility of cells. This extension allows for a concise description of the ``walking equivalence'' as a context, and of a set of maps characterising $\omega$-equifibrations as substitutions. We provide an implementation of our theory, which we use to formalise basic properties of invertible cells. These properties allow us to give semantics of ICaTT in marked weak $\omega$-categories, building a fibrant marked $\omega$-category out of every model of ICaTT.

papers.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

papers.title: Classification of some $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank 6
papers.abstract: A fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ is said to be $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic if the group $G(\mathcal{C})$ of invertible objects is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and the remaining simple objects form an orbit under the action of $G(\mathcal{C})$. In this paper, we give a partial classification of spherical $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank six. More precisely, we show that its Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}_0(\mathcal{C})$ must be one of nine fusion rings if the fusion rule multiplicities are less than $20$, and the categorifications of five of them are previously known. We prove that one of the last four fusion rings can be realized as de-equivariantization of a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}+8$.

papers.title: A convenient category of locales
papers.abstract: The notion of Kan extendable subcategories was initially introduced to define the category of compactly generated fibrewise topological spaces over a T1 base space and to establish its cartesian closure. In this paper, we show that the same framework can likewise be applied to define the category of compactly generated strongly Hausdorff locales and to prove that it, too, is cartesian closed

papers.title: Shape theory for condensed anima
papers.abstract: We give different perspectives on the notion of shape for condensed anima. We prove that it recovers more classical notions of shape not only for all locally compact Hausdorff but also locally contractible spaces. These recovering statements imply and extend comparison results on sheaf and condensed cohomology by Clausen-Scholze and Haine. Another homotopy-theoretical direction for condensed anima are their condensed homotopy groups. Connected to this, we give a description of the underlying topological group functor on condensed groups via quasi-topological groups.

papers.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
papers.abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.
